title: Shadow traffic request redaction prototypes (prompt/context artifacts) — working notes
content:
Context / why this doc exists
- Shadow traffic duplicates sampled production requests to candidate variants and scores outputs async. To debug/interpret metrics we need enough context, but must minimize sensitive data exposure.
- This doc captures prototype redaction approaches for storing shadow artifacts (prompt, system messages, tool args, retrieved context snippets, etc.) and notes where we expect false positives/false negatives.
- Primary use: inform ENG-5411 implementation defaults + security review.

Non-goals (for this doc)
- Solving perfect PII detection. We need "good defaults" with clear escape hatches + auditability.
- Full DLP solution. We are not building customer-custom classifiers in v1.

Assumptions (v1)
- Default retention is short (hours to days) and artifacts are access-controlled.
- Artifacts may be stored in multiple places depending on deployment mode:
  - Hosted/Dedicated: Redwood-managed storage
  - Private: customer-managed storage; Redwood provides config knobs + guidance
- Shadow scoring should not require raw prompt text for all metrics. Many metrics can run on model output only, or on "minimized" inputs.

What we are redacting
We deal with multiple request shapes:
1) Chat-like requests
- system: string
- messages[]: {role, content} where content is string or array of {type: text/image/tool_result}
- tools[] and tool_choice
2) Text generation
- prompt: string
3) Structured/JSON modes
- response_format / schema hints
- tool arguments: JSON-ish strings
4) Retrieved context / RAG
- documents[]: {title, url, snippet}

We also have metadata fields that can leak data indirectly:
- user_id / end_user_id (customer-supplied)
- conversation_id, ticket_id, email subject, URL query params
- custom headers

Prototypes

Prototype A — Regex-based scrubber (fast path, best-effort)
Summary
- Apply ordered regex rules to free-text fields, replacing matches with typed tokens.
- Keep a small allowlist of high-signal but generally low-risk features (lengths, language ID, token counts) for scoring/analytics.

Where applied
- prompt
- system
- messages[].content (text only)
- retrieved context snippets
- tool arguments (stringified JSON) as raw string pass

Default replacement format
- Replace with bracketed tokens:
  - [REDACTED_EMAIL]
  - [REDACTED_PHONE]
  - [REDACTED_SSN]
  - [REDACTED_CREDIT_CARD]
  - [REDACTED_IP]
  - [REDACTED_API_KEY]
  - [REDACTED_URL_QUERY]
  - [REDACTED_ADDRESS] (very weak; see notes)
- Do not preserve original length by default (length leakage is still leakage, but is much less than raw value). We do preserve total field length + token count separately.

Candidate regex rules (v0 list; not exhaustive)
- Email
  - (?i)\b[A-Z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Z0-9.-]+\.[A-Z]{2,}\b
- Phone (US-ish)
  - \b(?:\+?1[-.\s]?)?\(?\d{3}\)?[-.\s]?\d{3}[-.\s]?\d{4}\b
- SSN (US)
  - \b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b
- Credit card (very FP-prone; only with Luhn check)
  - \b(?:\d[ -]*?){13,19}\b  + Luhn validation
- IPv4
  - \b(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|[01]?\d\d?)\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4]\d|[01]?\d\d?)\b
- IPv6 (simplified)
  - \b(?:[A-F0-9]{1,4}:){7}[A-F0-9]{1,4}\b (case-insensitive)
- API keys / secrets (heuristic)
  - Common prefixes: sk-, rk-, xoxb-, xoxa-, ghp_, AKIA, etc.
  - High-entropy base64/hex strings of length >= 32 when near keywords ("token", "secret", "apikey")
- URLs: redact query params but preserve domain/path
  - Parse URL; keep scheme + host + path; replace query with ?[REDACTED_QUERY]

Pros
- Cheap (CPU), deterministic, easy to reason about.
- Works across arbitrary text without schema.

Cons / expected failure modes
- False negatives:
  - Names, free-form addresses, internal IDs, rare formats.
  - Non-US phone/ID formats.
  - Secrets without known prefix and without nearby keywords.
- False positives:
  - Any long number sequence triggers credit card candidate; mitigated with Luhn.
  - IPv4 patterns can match version numbers (e.g., "1.2.3.4" in docs).
- Regex will not handle structured tool args reliably (e.g., JSON with nested fields) without parsing.

Recommendation
- Prototype A is a required baseline, but should be layered with schema-aware redaction for tool args / metadata.


Prototype B — Structured allowlist + drop-everything-else (schema-first)
Summary
- Parse request into known structured fields and only persist a minimal allowlist for each request type.
- Store redacted free-text separately only when explicitly enabled.

Allowlist proposal (draft)
- Common
  - request_fingerprint_hash (already in routing bucketing)
  - timestamp, route_id, experiment_id
  - model_id_control, model_id_shadow
  - token counts (prompt_tokens, output_tokens)
  - language_id (fast CLD3/langid), safety classifier label (coarse)
- Chat/text
  - message_count
  - role sequence (e.g., "system,user,user,assistant")
  - first_user_message_truncated_and_redacted (optional; see Prototype C)
- Tool calling
  - tool_names (list)
  - tool_call_count
  - tool_argument_keys (only keys, not values)
- RAG
  - top_k
  - doc_ids_hashes (hash only)
  - doc_source_domains (if URLs present, domain only)

Where it fits
- Hosted/Dedicated default should be allowlist-only in the artifact store that powers aggregate metrics.
- For "example drilldown" UX, optionally store a separate "debug artifact" with stricter access controls + shorter retention.

Pros
- Strongest risk reduction; easiest to explain in security review.
- Predictable storage cost.

Cons / product impact
- Harder to debug regressions without seeing some prompt/output pairs.
- Some eval templates need limited prompt context (format instructions, schema hints).

Expected false positives/negatives
- This approach is conservative: it creates "false negatives" for debugging (we lose info) rather than "false negatives" for redaction.
- Main risk is product usability rather than data leakage.

Recommendation
- Use as default persistence model for metrics pipeline; pair with controlled debug artifacts (Prototype C).


Prototype C — Two-tier artifact model (metrics vs debug) with minimization
Summary
- Tier 1 (Metrics Artifact): allowlist-only (Prototype B). Default retention 24h.
- Tier 2 (Debug Artifact): redacted text + sampled raw excerpts. Default retention 4h (or disabled), stricter RBAC, explicit customer opt-in in Hosted/Dedicated, and per-tenant toggles.

Debug artifact contents (proposal)
- Redacted prompt/system/messages (Prototype A applied)
- Optional: "safe excerpt" capturing first N chars (e.g., 256–512) AFTER redaction.
- Optional: keep formatting tokens (newlines, markdown fences) to debug format adherence.
- Do not store full retrieved documents; only store snippet lengths and domains; optionally store redacted snippet excerpt.

Controls
- Per-tenant config: enable_debug_artifacts=true/false
- Per-route override: allow_debug_artifacts (default false)
- Sampling: debug_artifacts_sample_rate <= shadow_sample_rate (often much smaller, e.g., 0.01%)
- Hard caps:
  - Max bytes per artifact
  - Truncate each text field
  - Reject + record reason if artifact too large

Pros
- Gives Console "example drilldowns" without making raw text storage the default.
- Limits blast radius of mistakes.

Cons / risks
- Users may assume redaction is perfect; it’s not. UI must warn.
- Even redacted text can leak sensitive info via context ("my account is at Bank X"), or via unique phrases.

False positives/negatives to expect
- False negatives (leakage): names, addresses, unique identifiers not caught by regex.
- False positives: overly aggressive secret heuristics can mask non-sensitive tokens and reduce debugging usefulness.

Recommendation
- This seems like the best pragmatic approach for v1 (aligns with product needs + risk posture).


Prototype D — Field-level hashing + reversible encryption for select fields
Summary
- For certain identifiers, store only hashes (HMAC) so we can join and dedupe without storing raw.
- For extremely restricted cases, store encrypted payloads with short TTL and audited access.

Hashing details (proposal)
- Use HMAC-SHA256 with per-tenant key (from KMS) so hashes are not cross-tenant joinable.
- Fields:
  - end_user_id -> end_user_id_hmac
  - conversation_id -> conversation_id_hmac
  - customer-supplied request_id -> request_id_hmac
  - document IDs -> doc_id_hmac

Encryption (optional; likely defer)
- Envelope encryption with KMS key; decrypt only via audited workflow.
- This is heavyweight for v1; mention for regulated enterprise asks.

Pros
- Enables grouping/diagnosis without storing raw identifiers.

Cons
- Key management complexity, especially in Private.
- Doesn’t solve free-text leakage.

Recommendation
- Hashing: yes (low overhead, high value).
- Encryption: defer unless demanded by Private/regulated deals.


Prototype E — "PII classifier" gating (heuristic / lightweight ML)
Summary
- Run a lightweight PII detection model (or rules+heuristics) to decide whether to store debug artifacts at all.
- If classified as high-risk, store only Tier 1 metrics artifact.

Notes
- We should be careful: classifiers have both FP (blocks debugging too much) and FN (leakage).
- Might be best as an additional safety net rather than a primary mechanism.

Recommendation
- Defer to v2 unless we find a cheap, reliable option already used elsewhere in Redwood.


Specific redaction rules by field (draft)
1) Request metadata
- Drop: all custom headers by default.
- Keep (hashed): end_user_id, conversation_id.
- Keep (plain): route_id, experiment_id, region.

2) Prompt/messages text
- Apply regex scrubber.
- Then truncate.
- Then compute:
  - prompt_char_count
  - prompt_token_count
  - contains_code_block (heuristic)
  - contains_json (heuristic)

3) Tool args
- If tool args are JSON:
  - Parse -> keep keys only, values dropped.
  - If parse fails -> treat as text and run regex scrubber, then truncate.
- Special case: known built-in tools (e.g., retrieval.search, rerank): allowlist safe numeric params (top_k) but drop query strings.

4) RAG documents
- Default: keep domain + doc_id_hmac only.
- Optional debug: redacted + truncated snippet excerpt (strongly sample-gated).


Redaction test set ideas (we need to implement)
- Synthetic PII prompt corpus for unit tests:
  - emails/phones in multiple formats
  - secret-like strings with and without keywords
  - URL queries with tokens
  - non-PII long numbers that should not be redacted (invoice numbers, order IDs) — to measure FP
- Real-ish traffic snippets (internal dogfood only), manually reviewed, to estimate leakage.

How we should measure effectiveness (practical)
- Redaction coverage rate: percent of known PII patterns removed in synthetic corpus.
- False positive rate: percent of "clean" prompts that get heavily tokenized.
- Residual risk checklist: confirm we never store headers, never store raw end_user_id, etc.

Known tricky cases / notes
- Addresses and names are extremely hard with regex. We should NOT pretend to fully redact those.
- Multilingual: PII patterns vary. Email/phone ok; IDs less so.
- Tool args can embed full user input; schema-first redaction is critical.
- Even if we redact the prompt, the MODEL OUTPUT might echo sensitive user info. We need output redaction too (out of scope for this doc but should be symmetrical in implementation).

Open questions
- What’s the minimum debug artifact we need for Console example drilldowns to be useful?
- Should debug artifacts be available only to org admins by default?
- What is the default retention for debug artifacts in Dedicated? (My vote: off by default; enable per tenant during rollout windows.)
- Do we need a "customer-provided regex" facility? (Security risk; likely no for v1.)

Proposed v1 defaults (recommendation to bring to security review)
- Tier 1 metrics artifacts: allowlist-only (no raw text). Retention 24h (Hosted), configurable (Dedicated/Private).
- Tier 2 debug artifacts: OFF by default; when enabled:
  - regex scrubber + key-only tool args + URL query redaction
  - truncation caps
  - low sampling rate (<= 0.01% recommended)
  - retention 4h default
  - strict RBAC + audit logs for access
- Hash identifiers with per-tenant HMAC key.

Next steps / TODO
- [Benji] Turn regex list into actual shared library rules + benchmark CPU cost (ENG-5411)
- [Marcus/Kevin] Confirm RBAC + audit requirements for viewing debug artifacts in Console
- [Logan/Nadia] Validate that metrics pipeline does not require raw text fields (or document any exceptions)
- [All] Create synthetic test corpus + add to CI so rule changes are reviewed

Appendix: quick examples (illustrative)
1) Input: "Email me at jane.doe@acme.com about ticket 883-22-9911"
- Output: "Email me at [REDACTED_EMAIL] about ticket 883-22-9911" (ticket unchanged; might be sensitive but we don’t detect)

2) Input: "Authorization: Bearer sk-ABCD..." (in header)
- Stored: header dropped entirely (preferred) rather than relying on regex.

3) Tool args JSON: {"query":"customer SSN 123-45-6789", "top_k": 5}
- Stored keys: ["query","top_k"], stored numeric: top_k=5, query dropped (or stored only as [REDACTED_TEXT] if debug enabled)
